cpo.label: Crude palm oil (benchmark)
cpo.basis: World Bank Pink Sheet (S1), palm oil Malaysia crude/RBD, USD/t annual averages: FY2023A 886, FY2024A 963, FY2025A 1007; 2026 tape Q1 1081, Q2 1164, Q3 1148, July 1133, August 1132, September 1180. The World Bank re-based the palm oil series from January 2026 (S1 series note), so pre-2026 annual averages and the 2026 monthly tape are not perfectly homogeneous. Spot 1180 is the September-2026 monthly Pink Sheet print (S1). FY2026E 1135 takes the nine-month 2026 Pink Sheet average (1131 = mean of Q1 1081, Q2 1164, Q3 1148) and holds a firm Q4, itself bracketed by the Indonesia October-2026 CPO reference price (Harga Referensi, Kemendag) of US$1,042.15/t (S8, S9) - struck off a 20 Aug to 19 Sep window that printed Bursa CPO Malaysia US$1,145.42/t and Rotterdam US$1,526.56/t - and the rising Nov-Dec Bursa Malaysia FCPO strip (S2, S4). FY2027E 1240 anchors to the quoted forward strip: the FCPO curve is in backwardation, Nov-2026 RM4,587, Dec-2026 RM4,733, Jan-2027 RM4,818 rising to RM5,030 for Apr-2027 (S4), and RM5,022 to RM5,034 for May-Jul 2027 (S3), about 10 percent above the Nov-2026 contract, with the 2026-27 El Nino expected to hit 2027 FFB yields (S3) and MPOC guiding CPO above RM4,600 and RM4,700 (S5, S6); applied to the Kemendag-published Bursa Malaysia USD level (US$1,145.42, S8) the strip implies roughly US$1,240/t. FY2028E 1210 and FY2029E 1180 glide from the El Nino-inflated 2027 back toward the through-cycle as the weather deficit clears and Malaysian and Indonesian output and stocks normalise (S3). lt 1150 is the through-cycle anchor in FY2029 money: the 2026 Pink Sheet tape (about 1131, S1) plus the structural biodiesel bid (Indonesia B40 toward B50, Malaysia B20) and recurring El Nino supply risk (S3, S5), i.e. above the 2023-25 realised average (about 945) rather than reverting to it. lt_escalation is idr: PLANTATIONS is the one industry priced in USD and costed in IDR (fund record, unit_factor 0.001), so the USD/t CPO anchor must rise with the Indonesian rupiah cost base it is set against rather than with US inflation, preserving the USD margin over IDR costs. Realisation wedge for analysts: Indonesia applies an October-2026 export duty (BK) of US$178/t plus a 12.5 percent export levy (US$130.269/t) on the US$1,042.15/t reference price (S7, S8).

newc.label: Newcastle 6,000 kcal/kg NAR thermal coal
newc.basis: Actuals are the World Bank Pink Sheet (S23, October-2026 edition): Australian thermal coal f.o.b. Newcastle, 6,000 kcal/kg, annual averages FY2024A 136.1 and FY2025A 108.4 US$/t, with 2026 quarterly assessments Q1 122.3, Q2 135.4, Q3 138.1. Spot is the 2026-10-14 Newcastle October-2026 contract print (US$150.35/t, S19). FY2026E 137.0 blends nine months of Pink Sheet 2026 tape (~131.9 average) with the quoted Q4 forward curve (Oct-2026 149.35-150.35, Nov-2026 151.55-151.75, Dec-2026 152.75-153.30, S8/S19): the war-premium bid, China output curbs and Indonesia RKAB/drought supply discipline (S3, S7, S8, S22, S27) hold the year well above the 2025 average. The standing 146.5 estimate predated the Pink Sheet 2026 tape and is superseded. FY2027E ~118 assumes mean reversion as China mines restart (S3), Indonesian output runs near the ~700-720mt RKAB level (S27) and India/Vietnam demand normalises; the flag that spot 150.35 sits ~27% above FY2027E 118 is the war-premium carry, not a level the desk expects to persist. The ~110/105 path and lt 105 track flat-to-falling long-run thermal demand outside a sustained Iran-war premium, where marginal Indonesian supply historically clears near US$100-110/t on 6,000 NAR. Long-run escalation is usd: lt is a FY2029-money USD/t seaborne market-price anchor set against USD-denominated marginal supply costs, so it should preserve real value with m.inflation_usd_lt once the macro desk's scalar is in place. LESSON-0001 in force: commodity complex repriced; war premium intact.

ici4.label: Indonesian Coal Index 4 (4,200 kcal/kg GAR)
ici4.basis: No archivable public print this window. The Argus/Coalindo Indonesian Coal Index (ICI 1-5) is a proprietary subscriber product produced jointly by Argus Media Ltd and PT Coalindo Energy (ICI 4 = 4,200 kcal/kg GAR) and published only in the paid Argus/Coalindo report (S28, S31); the Coalindo site carries no public quote for the index level. The ICI-4 ~US$75/t figure quoted in industry-body commentary (IMEF chair to Bloomberg Technoz via S27) is a scenario projection tied to a proposed 700mt RKAB 2027 quota, not a published index level, so no spot is stated rather than estimated. ici3.basis: No archivable public print this window. hba.label: Harga Batubara Acuan (government reference price)
hba.basis: High-GAR HBA (6,322 kcal/kg) is set twice-monthly by Kepmen ESDM and is the export pricing floor since 1 Mar 2025 (Kepmen 384.K/MB.01/MEM.B/2026 for Oct-I 122.52, S1; Kepmen 401.K/MB.01/MEM.B/2026 for Oct-II 126.81, S14; Jul-II: 131.85 high-GAR / 89.90 I / 63.25 II / 45.08 III, S11). Spot is the latest archived decree print (Oct-II 2026, S14). No full FY actual series in one archivable table, so no FYyyyyA stated. Forward path tracks newc with the observed HBA/high-GAR-to-Newcastle spread (Oct 2026: HBA-II 126.81 vs NEWC Oct ~149.35-150.35, i.e. ~0.84x), normalised as the 2026 tightness abates toward the newc lt view. Long-run escalation is usd: HBA is a USD/t reference derived from coal market indices rather than a fixed nominal administered price, and lt follows the same USD-denominated through-cycle anchor as newc; m.inflation_usd_lt therefore applies once the macro desk's scalar is in place.

dmo_cap.label: DMO price cap for coal sold to power plants
dmo_cap.basis: Policy cap, not a market price: the DMO cap for the national electricity sector is a standing regulatory ceiling (MEMR Decree 261 K/30/MEM/2019, still USD 70/t FOB for 6,322 kcal/kg GAR in 2020, S2; reconfirmed current at USD 70/t for power in Jul-2026 industry reporting, S6). DMO for smelter/cement/fertilizer sits at USD 90/t (S6). No forecast path other than the standing cap (lt 70.0); any revision is a policy decision, not estimated. Long-run escalation is none: USD 70/t is a fixed nominal regulatory ceiling with no automatic inflation indexation, so only a new policy decision changes it.

hba_i.label: HBA I — reference price for 5,300 kcal/kg GAR coal
hba_i.basis: HBA I is set twice-monthly by Kepmen ESDM alongside the high-GAR HBA. Spot is the Period-II October 2026 print (Kepmen 401.K/MB.01/MEM.B/2026, effective 15 Oct 2026): HBA I 5,300 kcal/kg GAR = US$93.62/t, reported in the same decree article as the deck high-GAR spot 126.81 (S25, S14). Prior period (Oct-I, Kepmen 384.K/MB.01/MEM.B/2026) was US$90.60 (S24, S27); it tracks the high-GAR HBA with the observed grade spread (Jul-II: 131.85 high-GAR vs 89.90 I, S11). No forecast path; the desk re-prints the governing decree each period.

usd_idr.label: IDR per USD
usd_idr.basis: Desk review 2026-10-26 (MACRO_FX): FY2021A–FY2025A are Yahoo IDR=X daily-close fiscal-year averages (history_source); FY2026E 17,570 keeps the deterministic convention (year-to-date average blended with the reviewed spot 18,080, rounded — the seeded 17,546.8045 used the Yahoo placeholder spot 17,956). Spot is the reviewed onshore close Rp18,080/USD on 23-Oct-2026 (S7; corroborated S10). The desk rejects the Yahoo IDR=X placeholder (17,956 asof 25-Oct, ~0.7% below the onshore close) as stale/offshore and non-citable. FY2027E 18,350 (+1.5% vs spot), FY2028E 18,600, FY2029E 18,850, lt 19,000 (~+2.4%/yr trend) are desk judgment on the held balance_of_payments_pressure / CAUTIOUS regime: IDR weakens on a persistent current-account deficit (elevated oil import bill, Brent ~100–107/bbl per S8) and a narrowed carry gap (BI-Rate 5.75% on hold per S4 vs USD effective ~3.88% after the Sep-2026 Fed +25bp hike), with MSCI standalone-review risk keeping foreign portfolio flows a headwind (per S11, IHSG −11.6% on the MSCI proposal) and BI intervention capping the pace. The futures-broker projection inside S7 was quarantined and not used. Deck mode 2026-10-26 (MACRO_FX): `lt_escalation: ppp` set — IDR/USD is quoted rupiah-per-dollar, so after the last explicit year (FY2029E) the path must drift with the inflation gap for nominal consistency (the engine grows `lt` at (1+i_idr)/(1+i_usd)−1, ~+0.49%/yr on the sourced long-run anchors BI 2.5% vs Fed 2.0%), not `none` (which would pin a flat nominal rate while IDR costs still escalate at 2.5%, implying perpetual real IDR appreciation — the wrong sign for a held balance_of_payments_pressure regime). Note the explicit path runs faster than ppp (FY2026E 17,570→FY2029E 18,850 ≈ +2.4%/yr): the deck places the real IDR depreciation from the current-account deficit in the transition years and reverts to inflation-gap-only (real-flat) drift in the long run, i.e. ppp is the long-run steady state, the faster slide is the transition.

dxy.label: US dollar index
dxy.basis: Desk review 2026-10-26 (MACRO_FX): FY2021A–FY2025A are Yahoo DX-Y.NYB daily-close fiscal-year averages (history_source); FY2026E 99.9535 keeps the deterministic convention (year-to-date average blended with the Yahoo spot 101.81). Spot stays the Yahoo DX-Y.NYB close 101.81 asof 23-Oct-2026 — no citable archived print at that date was reachable this session. Corroborating context from archived press: DXY closed 102.58 on 12-Oct-2026, an 18-month high (S8), and 102 on 19-Oct-2026 (S11) — inside the ~2% band of the Yahoo spot, so no correction was applied. Both were left out of `sources` because their `published` fields are unset (the engine accepts reviewed variables without an evidence quote when history_source is present). FY2027E 102.25, FY2028E 102.0, lt 102.0 are desk judgment on the held balance_of_payments_pressure / CAUTIOUS regime: the USD stays firm at/near its highs — a hawkish Fed that hiked +25bp in Sep-2026 with a further hike live (S8), a war-premium oil bid and safe-haven demand (S8) — easing only gradually to a ~102.0 long-run level as US real rates and the war premium fade. Quarantined: the S8/S11 and other press carry analyst/broker FX projections (e.g. DXY to 104); none were used.

gold.label: Gold
gold.basis: Actuals are the World Bank Pink Sheet (S2, October-2026 edition, published 2026-10-02): gold spot average of daily rates, annual averages FY2023A 1,943, FY2024A 2,388 and FY2025A 3,442 US$/oz, with the 2026 quarterly tape Q1 4,876, Q2 4,512, Q3 4,268 and the September 2026 monthly print 4,319 (S2). Spot is the latest Pink Sheet monthly print (Sep 2026 US$4,319/oz, S2); it supersedes the unreviewed Yahoo GC=F seed (4,029.7) as the desk's sourced print. FY2026E 4,493.75 is the four 2026 Pink Sheet averages with Q4 set at the Sep-2026 print: nine months of tape average 4,552 and the year runs well above FY2025A 3,442 on central-bank and ETF demand. No liquid COMEX/LBMA forward or GOFO/lease strip could be archived this window (news discovery returned only broker commentary, excluded by the consensus quarantine), so the forecast path is anchored to the World Bank Commodity Markets Outlook April 2026 forecast (S4): 2026f 4,700, 2027f 4,300. The FY2026E tape blend supersedes the April 2026f because Q3-2026 spot has corrected ~17% from the Q1 peak. FY2027E 4,300 is the WB 2027f; FY2028E/FY2029E/lt 4,300 hold that level in real terms as the through-cycle anchor (no posted forward exists beyond the nearby strip; the WB forecast is the named public series). lt_escalation is usd: gold is a USD-denominated price set against USD-cost marginal supply, so lt should rise with m.inflation_usd_lt once the macro desk's scalar is in place. Spot 4,319 sits ~0.4% above FY2027E 4,300 (no drift flag). LESSON-0001 in force: commodity complex repriced.

brent.label: Brent crude
brent.basis: Actuals are the World Bank Pink Sheet (S1, October-2026 edition): Brent crude annual averages FY2023A 82.6, FY2024A 80.7 and FY2025A 69.0 US$/bbl, superseding the pre-review Yahoo-carried placeholders; pre-2023 actuals are omitted — no archivable primary print this session. Spot is the Friday-2026-10-23 settlement close (US$117.38/bbl, S8; EIA Europe Brent spot FOB last print US$115.22 on 2026-10-20, S4). FY2026E 96.0 blends nine months of 2026 tape (Pink Sheet Jan-Sep average ~93.7) with the EIA October-2026 STEO Q4 average of US$105/bbl (S11) under the current Saudi-Houthi / Strait-of-Hormuz supply-risk bid (S2, S3, S8): the Q4 market print runs ~114-120 against the STEO US$105 assumption. FY2027E 84.0 follows the EIA STEO 2027 annual average of US$84/bbl Brent (S11). FY2028E/FY2029E and lt 75 track a mean-reversion band above the 2025 average while the Iran-adjacent supply overhang persists, per the STEO assumption that Middle-East flows rebuild only gradually (S10, S11). Long-run escalation is usd: lt is a FY2029-money USD/bbl global market-price anchor set against USD-denominated supply costs, so it should preserve real value with m.inflation_usd_lt once the macro desk's scalar is in place. FY2028E/FY2029E and lt 3.1 hold near the STEO 2027 level on the same inventory-versus-LNG-export balance.

icp.label: Indonesian Crude Price (ICP)
icp.basis: Spot-series ICP is set monthly by Kepmen ESDM. Spot is the September-2026 monthly ICP of US$112.81/bbl, +US$23.38 vs August US$89.43/bbl, per Kepmen ESDM 395.K/MG.03/MEM.M/2026 reported via investor.id (S2); the same print is carried in the Oct-2026 industry.co.id close report (S8). No FYyyyyA is stated: the monthly Kepmen prints are archived (Dec-2025 US$61.10, Nov-2025 US$62.83, S12) but no full-year ESDM average is published in one archivable table this session, so no annual actual is estimated. FY2026E 92.0 is the ESDM-reported January-October 2026 ICP average of US$91-92/bbl stated by Minister Bahlil to the press on 19 Oct 2026 (S9) — a realised ten-month average, carried as FY2026E rather than a forecast (corroborated by the Jan-May 2026 average of US$91.86/bbl from the ESDM monthly series, S14). FY2027E 78.0 positions between the FY2026E realised average and the STEO-anchored Brent 2027 view (~84, S11) given ICP's discount to the Brent/WTI benchmarks observed in the September decree (S2). FY2028E/FY2029E and lt 69 converge toward the pre-war ICP/APBN band (APBN 2026 assumption US$70/bbl, S14). LESSON-0001 in force: war-premium tape intact.
